name: Dockside Cold-Chain Handler's Day Rig
description: Built for the refrigerated cargo holds and cold-chain loading bays of Meridian Harbor's bulk freight terminals, this layered kit prioritizes thermal retention without sacrificing the freedom of movement needed to work a full shift. The outermost layer is a high-collar insulated vest in safety orange with black ripstop side panels, harbor authority reflective striping at the shoulders, and a large patch pocket on the chest marked with the worker's dock assignment number in hand-written marker. Beneath the vest sits a heavyweight fleece-lined work shirt in deep navy, quarter-zip with a reinforced collar that folds high against wind off the lake. The shirt has a left-sleeve BCI port pass-through — a simple rubberized grommet that lets wrist-mounted interface hardware route cleanly without bunching fabric. Trousers are insulated canvas in charcoal with wide-set cargo pockets, boot-cut leg opening to clear ankle-height footwear, and neoprene knee pads sewn in permanently. Boots are waterproof pull-on dock boots with a steel toe, non-slip tread rated for wet deck surfaces, and a calf-height shaft. A thermal balaclava in navy rolls down to a neck gaiter when the bay doors are open.
functionality: thermal insulation for cold-chain environments, BCI port pass-through at left sleeve, non-slip waterproof steel-toe boot, neoprene knee pads, roll-down balaclava/neck gaiter, dock assignment patch system, reflective shoulder striping
what_it_says: Cold-chain work is specialist labor — not everyone can tolerate the hours in the freeze. This kit marks the wearer as someone who endures conditions most people avoid, and the handwritten dock assignment number on the chest pocket suggests a long tenure and a system that knows them by habit rather than name.
manufacturer: Meridian Harbor Authority (vest and balaclava, issued) / independent (shirt, trousers, boots, personal purchase from Circuit-level retailers)
price_range: Φ200–Φ310 (full kit, mix of issued and personal)
story_hooks: The dock assignment number on the chest patch belongs to a worker who transferred out two months ago — and someone has been using their credentials to access restricted cold-storage sections.
A cold-chain handler discovers a container that isn't on any manifest, packed with something that isn't food, buried under three layers of legitimate cargo.
The BCI port pass-through in the sleeve makes it easy to interface with dock management systems — but it also means a skilled slicer can read the worker's interface traffic if they get close enough.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian cold-chain worker silhouette — layered and blocky through the torso, tapered at the legs. High-visibility safety orange vest dominates the upper body, contrasted by navy underlayers. Broad shoulders squared by reinforced vest construction. The overall impression is built for function in freezing industrial spaces, not aesthetics.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately relaxed and loose-fitting to accommodate thermal layers beneath without compression. Cargo trousers sit at natural waist with room through hip and thigh. Vest drapes openly over the shirt. Boot-cut legs clear the ankles. Everything sized for freedom of movement during repetitive dock labor.
physical_description.primary_material: Ballistic ripstop (vest side panels), heavyweight insulated synthetic blend (vest shell), fleece-lined cotton-poly (work shirt), insulated canvas (trousers), thermoplastic-coated neoprene (integrated knee pads), rubber-soled steel-toe dock boot
physical_description.texture: Ripstop has a fine grid texture; vest shell is slightly quilted for insulation pockets. Fleece lining visible at shirt cuffs and collar — soft and brushed. Canvas trousers have a utilitarian weave. Neoprene knee pads are smooth and flexible. Boots have aggressive tread and sealed seams.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary safety orange (vest) with matte black ripstop accents on sides and underarms. Deep navy (fleece shirt, balaclava, knee pads). Charcoal canvas (trousers). Reflective silver/white striping at shoulders. Hand-written assignment number in fading marker on chest patch.
physical_description.closures: Vest: magnetic snaps and hidden friction-fit side straps. Shirt: quarter-zip with rubberized pull. Trousers: reinforced button fly with metal rivets at stress points. Boots: pull-on elastic gusset. Balaclava: none—rolls up or down as needed.
distinctive_features: Hand-written dock assignment marker on chest pocket (personalization/identification)
BCI port pass-through grommet on left sleeve—rubberized, designed for wrist-mounted interface hardware
Reflective authority striping in harbor-issue silver
Permanently sewn neoprene knee pads (visible wear expected)
Thermal balaclava that converts to neck gaiter
Black ripstop side panels for abrasion resistance during cargo handling
Wide cargo pockets for tools, gloves, thermal pack
Non-slip boot tread with steel toe cap
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class) — mixed issued and personal purchase. Vest and balaclava are workplace-provided; shirt, trousers, boots chosen from mid-tier Circuit-level retailers. Practical, durable, affordable.
physical_description.cultural_context: Meridian Harbor dock worker. Suggests someone embedded in the cold-chain logistics network of the GLMZ, likely with BCI augmentation for inventory management. Reflects the unglamorous backbone of urban cargo infrastructure. Wearing this signals labor identity, not status.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Chest pocket marker fades with shifts. Knee pads show creasing and minor scuff marks. Vest retains structure but edges soften from repeated folding. Boots carry salt residue and deck grime. No major tears, but patina of heavy use.

image_prompt: A cyberpunk dock worker in full cold-chain rig: safety-orange insulated vest with black ripstop panels and faded hand-written dock assignment number over heavyweight navy fleece-lined work shirt. Insulated charcoal cargo trousers with visible neoprene knee pads, pulled into waterproof steel-toe dock boots. Left sleeve shows the subtle rubberized BCI port pass-through grommet. Thermal navy balaclava draped around neck like a gaiter. Shot against a moody Meridian Harbor backdrop—refrigerated cargo container, frost-rimmed loading bay, dim amber and cool blue industrial lighting. Rain-slicked deck surface. Dark, utilitarian, worn but functional. Cinematic labor realism. --ar 2:3 --v 6
